concepts.title: Magic as the Second Self
concepts.excerpt: Most people carry a vague sense of the word. Something you do. Or a force out in the world you can tap into if you know the trick.

concepts.title: Why the Source Needs a First God
concepts.excerpt: Later on you get spells. Every one of them has you say a name out loud — an angel's name, a name of God, one of the ten stations on the Tree of Life.

concepts.title: The Four Worlds as an Operating Procedure
concepts.excerpt: Everybody has one. Something you worked out in full — you knew what it was, what it was for, roughly how it would go — and then you never said it to anyone and never started it.

concepts.title: The Four Worlds Hold Four Things
concepts.excerpt: Tin goes with Thursday. Iron goes with Mars, and with the throat, and with a particular archangel.

concepts.title: Space as a Sheet and Time as Its Wrinkles
concepts.excerpt: Take everything out of a room. The furniture, the air, the light. What is left is empty space, and most people would say that is the end of it — nothing there, and nothing under the nothing.

concepts.title: The Magical Spectrum
concepts.excerpt: Some things in this curriculum are handed to a beginner on day one. Others are stated to be out of reach for years, and a few are described as impossible for anybody at apprentice level.

concepts.title: The Archprimes
concepts.excerpt: The celestial side of this system has a clear chain of command. Archangels at the top, then intelligences, then princes, then ministering spirits — a named hierarchy you can address at any level.

concepts.title: The Two Hidden Pillars
concepts.excerpt: Every diagram of the Tree of Life shows three vertical pillars — Mercy on the right, Severity on the left, and the Golden or Middle Pillar down the centre.

concepts.title: Thirty-Two Universal Laws, and How to Nullify One
concepts.excerpt: Everything in creation, formation and manifestation is governed by a law, or rather by groups of laws.

concepts.title: The Eleven Primordial and Four Primary Forces
concepts.excerpt: Two forces and eight behaviours is a small kit — giving and taking, at four strengths each.

concepts.title: The Eight Universal Potentials
concepts.excerpt: Back in the cosmogony there were two forces with four behaviours each.

concepts.title: Additus and Nihilus — The Eight Verbs
concepts.excerpt: Seventy-eight incantations come later, spread across twelve categories and two levels.

concepts.title: The Octovium
concepts.excerpt: The justification offered is short and does a lot of work: magic, in itself, is the study of everything.

concepts.title: Philosophy as Magical Training
concepts.excerpt: The first of the eight disciplines is philosophy, and the reason given for studying it is not that it makes a person wise.

concepts.title: Mythology and the Ten Degrees of Divine Beings
concepts.excerpt: Suppose you want help with something and you have decided to ask a spirit for it.

concepts.title: Alchemy as the Third Discipline
concepts.excerpt: Everybody knows the story about turning lead into gold, and everybody knows it did not work.

concepts.title: Mathematics and the Quaternary
concepts.excerpt: Nobody expects a magical syllabus to send you back to sums. Astrology, yes.

concepts.title: Kabbalah as the Art of Receiving
concepts.excerpt: Prayer sends something up. That much everybody understands. The harder question is what comes back down, and how a person on this end would recognise it if it did.

concepts.title: Astrology and the Zodiacal-Sidereal Split
concepts.excerpt: You want to do a thing. Somebody tells you to wait until Thursday, and to use a piece of iron rather than a piece of copper, and to say a particular angel's name while you do it.

concepts.title: Sacred Geometry and the Built Matrices
concepts.excerpt: Draw a circle on the floor and stand in it. Nothing has been added to the room.

concepts.title: Illumination, Initiation, Ascension, Transenation
concepts.excerpt: Hundreds of pages of formulas, metals, stones, oils, drills and rosters, and somewhere behind all of it there has to be an answer to the plainest question a beginner could ask.

concepts.title: The Sphere Is a Thought-Form
concepts.excerpt: Not energy, and not anything borrowed. The Philosophical Sphere is made of thought, and specifically of yours.

concepts.title: The Philosophical Sphere Solves a Latency Problem
concepts.excerpt: Everything that manifests has to come down through four worlds in order — potential, then creation, then formation, then the physical.

concepts.title: The Quickening of the Philosophical Sphere
concepts.excerpt: Everything in the sphere chapter has been construction. Eight rings, sixty-four selected concepts, a geometry derived from bending the Tree into a circle.

concepts.title: The Four Cosmogonic Aspects in the Sphere
concepts.excerpt: The central instrument of this whole curriculum is not an object. It is a structure you build in your head and keep there — and the obvious objection is the one anybody would raise.

concepts.title: The Eight Magical Directions
concepts.excerpt: Most of what happens to a person arrives unannounced. A bill, an offer, somebody turning up, something breaking.

concepts.title: The Eight-Fold Manifold
concepts.excerpt: Count what this system hands you. Eight furnaces. Eight verbs. Eight universal potentials.

concepts.title: Two Power Supplies and a Gearbox
concepts.excerpt: From two places, and they don't mix on their own. Three of the sphere's rings run on you.

concepts.title: The Energy Economy of Philius and Neikos
concepts.excerpt: There are two answers and they belong to two different forces. Nihilus Philius takes from the universe and puts it in your sphere.

concepts.title: The Ring of Virtues
concepts.excerpt: Because in this system your conduct is a power supply.

concepts.title: The Ring of Values
concepts.excerpt: The third and last of the inner rings is for pressure.

concepts.title: The Ring of Statutes
concepts.excerpt: The first ring governs what happens inside you when something lands. This one governs everything that happens between you and somebody else.

concepts.title: The Ring of Deities
concepts.excerpt: The question gets answered before it's asked, and the answer is a distinction rather than a denial.

concepts.title: The Archetype Ring Buys Order by Shutting Doors
concepts.excerpt: Because something is arriving that you didn't choose, and it will leave again on its own schedule.

concepts.title: The Esophoros Ring and the Lumen Score
concepts.excerpt: Almost nothing in this curriculum gives you a number. Durations are vague, the sphere finishes when it finishes, and most drills end in a change of perception nobody could check.

concepts.title: The Eight Furnaces
concepts.excerpt: Every school in this system points at a spot on the body and says the magic goes out through there.

concepts.title: The Charge-and-Project Drill
concepts.excerpt: Read all ten school drills in a row and something becomes obvious that reading any one of them hides.

concepts.title: A Word Is a Number Is a Code
concepts.excerpt: Every operation in this system ends in speech. The four worlds cross into the physical on a spoken word.

concepts.title: Numbers as Broadcast Devices
concepts.excerpt: Go looking for the number five. Not five apples, not the digit written on a page — five itself.

concepts.title: Number One and the Monogram
concepts.excerpt: Count what is in front of you. A table, two chairs, a lamp. You can number all of it — and none of those numbers is for the space the things are sitting in.

concepts.title: The Radial Tension
concepts.excerpt: There is a person who will not answer your messages, or a situation stuck in disagreement, or a conversation that keeps failing.

concepts.title: Three and the Act of Synthesis
concepts.excerpt: A project that will not start. A conversation that has gone flat. A room that feels dead.

concepts.title: Number Four and the Tetractys
concepts.excerpt: Stand in a field with nothing in it. There is no north until somebody supplies one, no left, no far side.

concepts.title: The Elemental Pentagram and the Doctrine of Five
concepts.excerpt: There is a passage in the middle of this section that has nothing to do with stars or elements, and it is the most direct thing on the page.

concepts.title: Six and the Union of Opposites
concepts.excerpt: A room you walk into and immediately want to leave. A situation that has not gone wrong yet and already feels wrong.

concepts.title: The Seven-Pointed Star
concepts.excerpt: Seven days in a week. Seven colours in a rainbow. Seven metals in alchemy, seven candles on the menorah, seven days of creation, seven archangels, seven planets you can see with your eyes.

concepts.title: Nine, and What Will Not Descend by Itself
concepts.excerpt: You have the cosmology. You know which force does what, which world sits above which, which name belongs to which being.

concepts.title: The Ten Fingers as a Planetary Keyboard
concepts.excerpt: Every other operation here needs equipment. A wand, a consecrated censer, eight stones in a circle, a formula said out loud in a room with nobody else in it.

concepts.title: The Master Numbers
concepts.excerpt: The numbers chapter gives a grid for each digit from one to ten — objects laid out in a configuration, charged with a formula.

concepts.title: The Platonic Solids as Containers
concepts.excerpt: Most of the objects in this practice send something out. A grid broadcasts a number, a pentacle carries a written word, a wand releases what the sphere has gathered.

concepts.title: Four Weapons From Four Divine Essences
concepts.excerpt: An apprentice put that question to his teacher, and the answer came in two halves.

concepts.title: The Ladder of Weapons
concepts.excerpt: Nothing stops a person walking into a shop and buying a rod. It costs less than a sword and it takes less skill to carry.

concepts.title: Every Weapon Has a Shadow List
concepts.excerpt: Correspondence tables in occult books usually read one way. A planet, a metal, a colour, a set of qualities — all of them favourable, because the table exists to tell you what the thing is good for.

concepts.title: The Chalice Is a Curve
concepts.excerpt: Not for holding liquid. The mystery of the Chalice begins with its geometric form, and what follows is the strangest piece of reasoning in the whole weapons material.

concepts.title: The Uses and Types of Chalices
concepts.excerpt: Read the table and there are eight chalices, each with its own name and its own blessed liquid.

concepts.title: Why a Pentacle Is Written On
concepts.excerpt: The chalice holds liquid, the sword has an edge, the wand is a length of wood.

concepts.title: The Uses and Types of Pentacles
concepts.excerpt: Three of the four weapons work the same way. Own one cup, one sword, one wand, charge whichever aspect you need today, and the same object serves for everything.

concepts.title: The Sword and the Unseen
concepts.excerpt: Nothing in this curriculum asks you to fight anybody. The schools heal, bless, find things out, calm situations and call helpful beings.

concepts.title: The Uses and Types of Swords
concepts.excerpt: There is a moment in any dealing with something powerful where the question stops being what do I want and becomes why should it listen to me.

concepts.title: The Wand Carries All Four Worlds
concepts.excerpt: The chalice is water, the sword is air, the pentacle is earth. Each does its element's work, and reaching outside it means reaching for a different tool.

concepts.title: The Uses and Types of Wands
concepts.excerpt: Four weapons sit on the table. Three of them are optional on any given day.

concepts.title: Consecration Charges in Sunlight
concepts.excerpt: A chalice bought in a shop is a cup. A sword is a length of steel.

concepts.title: Gold and the Authority Set
concepts.excerpt: You can buy a planet at a jeweller's.

concepts.title: Silver Against the Undead
concepts.excerpt: Everybody knows the folklore. A silver bullet for the werewolf, a silver blade for the vampire.

concepts.title: Iron and the Weekly Body Pass
concepts.excerpt: The instruction is one sentence and it costs nothing.

concepts.title: Copper Draws and Lead Holds
concepts.excerpt: Copper is a conductor. Lead is a shield. Everything either metal does in this practice follows from that one physical difference, and the difference is used rather than illustrated.

concepts.title: Tin and the Jupiter Set
concepts.excerpt: Most of the working material in this curriculum aims at something specific.

concepts.title: Lead and the Saturn Set
concepts.excerpt: Not a crisis exactly. The stage before that — when a situation is getting out of control, becoming too difficult, turning dangerous or altogether perilous and precarious, and you can feel it sliding.

concepts.title: Mercury Withdrawn, Aluminium Substituted
concepts.excerpt: Seven metals, seven planets, one entry with a hole in it. Mercury is described, its properties are given — and then it is taken off the table.

concepts.title: Never Substitute One Metal for Another
concepts.excerpt: Go and look at the hallmark inside a ring. Sterling silver is 92. 5% silver and the rest is usually copper.

concepts.title: Every Stone Houses Someone
concepts.excerpt: Pick up the tumbled amethyst you bought in a shop. On this account you are holding a person's house.

concepts.title: The Cleansing That Differs From the Common One
concepts.excerpt: There is a step in this procedure that nothing else in the practice contains.

concepts.title: Programming Versus Enchanting
concepts.excerpt: Two pages earlier, a gemstone was a house with somebody living in it — a living, thinking, magical being to be approached with a silent prayer, informed of your purpose, promised not to be abused, and thanked afterwards for its cooperation.

concepts.title: Protective and Grounding Stones
concepts.excerpt: The stone lists here look like the ones in any crystal book until you notice what is attached to each heading.

concepts.title: Healing Stones by Organ
concepts.excerpt: Most writing about healing crystals tells you which stone is for which complaint and stops.

concepts.title: Communing and Energizing Stones
concepts.excerpt: The protective lists sort by threat and the healing lists sort by organ.

concepts.title: Four Days of Fasting for the Supreme Beings
concepts.excerpt: Almost nothing in this practice is hard to do. The drills are five and ten minutes.

concepts.title: Asking a Plant Before You Cut It
concepts.excerpt: There is a rosemary bush in a garden and a working that needs some of it.

concepts.title: Oils Carry Incantations to Other People
concepts.excerpt: Every other material in this practice is found. Stones come out of the earth, metals out of a jeweller's, plants out of a garden.

concepts.title: The Drop Counts Are Not Arbitrary
concepts.excerpt: Every oil recipe here specifies drops. Eight of mandrake, four of frankincense, two of dragon's blood.

concepts.title: Fumigation
concepts.excerpt: You work at a table in your study. Yesterday somebody argued in that room.

concepts.title: The Smoking Censer
concepts.excerpt: A crystal ball will tell you about distant places, the past and the future.

concepts.title: The Anatomy of a Candle
concepts.excerpt: Two on the altar. Four around a consecration. One lit before every operation.

concepts.title: The Altar and the Four Towers
concepts.excerpt: Every drill so far has said a quiet room. Nothing has said where you stand, what you stand at, or what keeps the room to yourself while you work.

concepts.title: The Hood Dissolves the Individual
concepts.excerpt: A surgeon scrubs and puts on the gown. A judge puts on the robe. A monk puts on the orange mantle.

concepts.title: The Water Vase
concepts.excerpt: Somebody has told you something and you do not believe it. You do not own a scrying ball, or you do and it is under linen halfway through its eleven days.

concepts.title: Scrying Devices Are Relay Points
concepts.excerpt: Somebody stares into a glass ball and says they can see a house. The obvious question is whether the house is in the glass.

concepts.title: The Eleven-Day Crystal
concepts.excerpt: A glass sphere arrives in the post. It is beautiful, it cost real money, and nothing happens when you look into it.

concepts.title: What the Drills Ask of the Senses
concepts.excerpt: Go through every exercise in this curriculum and ask what the practitioner is actually asked to do with their attention.

concepts.title: Odin Paid Twice for the Runes
concepts.excerpt: A god goes looking for wisdom and finds a giant at a well who will not give it away.

concepts.title: The Three Initiatic Keys
concepts.excerpt: A rune set has twenty-four signs in it and no obvious place to start. This material solves that by cutting the set into three groups of eight and naming each group after what it is for.

concepts.title: Reading Runes by Orientation
concepts.excerpt: Most rune books give you two: upright and reversed. This one gives three, and the third is where the whole reading system lives.

concepts.title: The Tarot as a Set of Talismans
concepts.excerpt: Every tarot entry here has a divinatory meanings field, which is what you expect.

concepts.title: Reading Your Own Name in Numbers
concepts.excerpt: Almost everything in this material is asserted rather than shown.

concepts.title: Choosing a Magical Name
concepts.excerpt: The clearest instruction in this whole section is a worked example with two names in it.

concepts.title: Celestial Names Are Verbs Plus EL
concepts.excerpt: Raphael, Michael, Gabriel, Camael, Tzaphkiel, Tzadkiel. Six names, one ending.

concepts.title: The Logos Across Four Traditions
concepts.excerpt: You can think a thing as hard as you like and nothing moves. Say it, and — on this account — something does.

concepts.title: The Four Magical Voices
concepts.excerpt: No — and the four voices are the answer to that question, one register each for four different kinds of work.

concepts.title: The Voice of Prayer
concepts.excerpt: Three of the four voices in this practice are for getting something done.

concepts.title: The Voice of Magic
concepts.excerpt: The words are printed. Anybody can read them off the page. So what is left to get wrong?

concepts.title: The Voice of Ceremony
concepts.excerpt: A wedding, a funeral, a harvest festival. There are people standing in the room, and the words are said out loud so they can hear them.

concepts.title: The Voice of Ritual
concepts.excerpt: Both are formulas, said out loud, often with other people in the room.

concepts.title: Fewer Words Reach Heaven Faster
concepts.excerpt: Incantations here come in three sizes, and the size is not a stylistic matter.

concepts.title: Magic Words Must Be in the Present Tense
concepts.excerpt: Because a request in the future tense doesn't stick. Words created in past or future tenses tend to get lost in the matrix of reality.

concepts.title: The Casting Syntax
concepts.excerpt: Everything else in this practice is preparation. This is the sentence you actually say, and its structure is given once, in one paragraph, with one worked example.

concepts.title: Six Conditions Before You Speak
concepts.excerpt: You have the formula. School words, incantation, magic word, in order.

concepts.title: The Psalm as a Power Source
concepts.excerpt: Open the spellbook at any entry and the same thing is sitting under the effect: a line of Latin, and a psalm number.

concepts.title: Magical Symbols, Somatic Movements and Sekinoth
concepts.excerpt: Read the spellbook and a working looks like a phrase, a psalm and a name.

concepts.title: The Formula Grammar
concepts.excerpt: Read the exorcisms one at a time and each looks like an ancient formula for its own substance.

concepts.title: The NN Slot
concepts.excerpt: In the middle of a Latin conjuration for water elementals, the sentence stops making sense.

concepts.title: Two Incantations Carry Everything
concepts.excerpt: A reader working through this material meets dozens of named incantations.

concepts.title: The Magical Levels of an Incantation
concepts.excerpt: Every incantation in the spellbook sits under a heading that says First Level or Second Level.

concepts.title: The Assistance Economy
concepts.excerpt: Every incantation in the spellbook carries a magical level, and a beginner will read that as a difficulty rating.

concepts.title: Orisons, Artificium, Conjurations and Rituals
concepts.excerpt: Every magical operation in this system is one of four sizes, and the sizes are strict enough that you can tell which one you're holding by counting the words.

concepts.title: The Anatomy of an Orison
concepts.excerpt: Not a rhetorical question. This system has a rule about it, and the rule decides what class a formula belongs to.

concepts.title: The Four Forms of Artificium
concepts.excerpt: You know a charm that clears up misunderstandings and another that steadies a room.

concepts.title: The Twelve Dimensions of a Conjuration
concepts.excerpt: Most of the working material here is small. Two or three Latin words, a psalm, an hour of the day.

concepts.title: The Liturgical Year
concepts.excerpt: Almost everything in this curriculum is done alone, when you need it. A fever arrives and you cast at it.

concepts.title: Greater Rituals and the Raising of the Temple
concepts.excerpt: Read four hundred pages of this material and the picture is consistent.

concepts.title: The Ten Schools as One Architecture
concepts.excerpt: Because there are almost eighty, and you're being given the ones that won't hurt you.

concepts.title: The School of Alterations
concepts.excerpt: Turning one thing into another is what most people picture when they picture magic.

concepts.title: The School of Benedictions
concepts.excerpt: Ten schools, and one of them is explicitly the place to begin.

concepts.title: The School of Divinations
concepts.excerpt: Some things you can look up. Some things you can work out.

concepts.title: The School of Enchantments
concepts.excerpt: This is the school that works on how people feel — charming, fascinating, enthralling and mesmerising them, changing what they like and how they're disposed towards a thing.

concepts.title: The School of Healings
concepts.excerpt: That's the question the whole school turns on, and it decides which of four things you're allowed to reach for.

concepts.title: The School of Invocations
concepts.excerpt: Nine of the ten schools have you do the work. This one has you ask somebody else to do it, and that changes the shape of everything — the categories, the drill, and what counts as success.

concepts.title: The School of Lights
concepts.excerpt: The invocation school calls heaven down to make things better — peace, consciousness, people reconciled.

concepts.title: The School of Naturals
concepts.excerpt: Every other school works on a person — you, or somebody in front of you, or something you own.

concepts.title: The School of Protections
concepts.excerpt: The obvious answer is people who mean you harm, and that's the smallest part of it here.

concepts.title: The School of Conjurations
concepts.excerpt: The second half of that question is normally the whole problem with summoning, and here it gets an answer flat enough to be startling.

concepts.title: First Level Alterations: Formos
concepts.excerpt: A project that will not start. A shop with no customers. A group losing people.

concepts.title: First Level Benedictions: Benedictus
concepts.excerpt: Every operation in this curriculum ends up touching an object. A cup, a stone, a piece of metal, a room.

concepts.title: First Level Divinations: Auguros
concepts.excerpt: Four charms open the divination school, and none of them is about the far future.

concepts.title: First Level Enchantments: Fascinos
concepts.excerpt: The enchantment school is the one aimed at people, and reading its first five together tells you where this system draws its lines — because four of the five carry a condition that decides whether the charm fires at all.

concepts.title: First Level Healing: Salve
concepts.excerpt: ⚠ Before anything else: nothing on this page is medical advice, and nothing here replaces a doctor.

concepts.title: First Level Invocations: Petos
concepts.excerpt: Most people who pray assume the thing arrives. The invocation school does not, and one of its four first-level charms exists for exactly that gap.

concepts.title: First Level Lights: Lucis
concepts.excerpt: Every school in this spellbook works on something. Alterations move situations, healings work on bodies, enchantments work on people.

concepts.title: First Level Naturals: Meteorikos
concepts.excerpt: Every other school in this spellbook can be worked in a quiet room. This one cannot, and the difference shows up in the instructions rather than in the effects.

concepts.title: First Level Protections: Auxilium
concepts.excerpt: Most charms in this spellbook say what they do. The protection school says what ends them, and the four failure conditions are more instructive than the four effects.

concepts.title: First Level Conjurations: Conjuratos
concepts.excerpt: Every other school in this spellbook produces an effect. This one produces a relationship, and the four entries spend more words on how to behave toward the being than on what the being does.

concepts.title: Second Level Alterations: Mutatios
concepts.excerpt: The first five alterations get things moving. The second five do something else, and reading them side by side shows what a level actually buys in this system.

concepts.title: Second Level Benedictions: Benedicci
concepts.excerpt: Most blessings, as people usually imagine them, are general. Good wishes, pointed at somebody, hoping for the best.

concepts.title: Second Level Divinations: Vates
concepts.excerpt: The first divinations handle the lost object and the person in front of you.

concepts.title: Second Level Enchantments: Ensalmos
concepts.excerpt: The first enchantments act on a person to help them. Three of these four act on a person who has already been acted on by somebody else — and the assumption behind all three is that the victim may not know.

concepts.title: Second Level Healing: Curo
concepts.excerpt: ⚠ Nothing on this page is medical advice and nothing here replaces medical care.

concepts.title: Second Level Invocations: Apelos
concepts.excerpt: This practice is solitary almost everywhere. One person in a quiet room, door shut, no non-magical people present.

concepts.title: Second Level Lights: Iluminos
concepts.excerpt: The first level of Lights turns a practitioner on and lets other people respond.

concepts.title: Second Level Naturals: Telurikos
concepts.excerpt: The first-level weather charms are for somebody caught out — a flood, a lightning storm, a field that needs rain.

concepts.title: Second Level Protections: Guardos
concepts.excerpt: The first-level protections build boundaries — a circle, six walls, a companion, a binding.

concepts.title: Second Level Conjurations: Conjuros
concepts.excerpt: The first-level conjurations all end in an object. A water elemental kept sweet by daily casting, a river spirit housed in a receptacle you must never be parted from, a dwarf given a nice gemstone.

concepts.title: The Wizardly Trades
concepts.excerpt: Nobody can study everything. The Octovium alone is eight full disciplines in original editions, the ten schools each have eight degrees, and there are seventy more schools after that.

concepts.title: The Arcanist
concepts.excerpt: Somebody hands you a formula and says it does a particular thing. How does anybody know?

concepts.title: The Bestiologist
concepts.excerpt: Here is a claim that sounds like it cannot be right. Learn more about a creature and you are more likely to succeed at calling it.

concepts.title: The Conjurer
concepts.excerpt: Say you need something guarded overnight. You could call whatever is nearest and hope it holds.

concepts.title: The Diviner
concepts.excerpt: Some questions have no witness. What happened in a room fifty years ago with everyone in it now dead.

concepts.title: The Healer
concepts.excerpt: A person in front of you is sick. Not metaphorically — a fever, a wound, something that has taken a function away.

concepts.title: The Kabbalist
concepts.excerpt: Every working in this curriculum ends the same way. You say a name.

concepts.title: The Magus
concepts.excerpt: Nine of the ten trades do something. They test formulas, catalogue creatures, call spirits, read cards, heal people, fight things, run rites.

concepts.title: The Planemaster
concepts.excerpt: You call something. It comes, it does the job, you dismiss it. Then what?

concepts.title: The Praetor
concepts.excerpt: One footnote does a piece of work that the main text does not, and it corrects a reader's likely assumption before they can make it.

concepts.title: The Templar
concepts.excerpt: Every ceremony in this curriculum arrives finished. A formula, a psalm, an hour, a set of names, a sequence of circuits around a room.

concepts.title: What the System Says It Cannot Do
concepts.excerpt: Buried in the spellbook, attached to a charm for calming animals, is one of the strangest sentences in the whole curriculum.

concepts.title: Disclosure Severs the Channel
concepts.excerpt: You have used an incantation to obtain knowledge, and now you want to tell somebody what you found out.

concepts.title: The Cosmic Consciousnesses
concepts.excerpt: The strangest thing about this material is that it sits in an appendix, and the strangeness is admitted on the spot.

concepts.title: The Practice of the Consciousnesses
concepts.excerpt: Almost everything in this curriculum has a procedure. Words to say, an hour to wait for, a metal to hold, a circle to draw, a stone to charge.

concepts.title: Epistemic Discipline and Noise Filtering
concepts.excerpt: Strategy 25 (Ignore the Barking Dog That Hunts) presents a simple principle with profound implications: don't get drawn into irrelevant conflicts.
